ever exist. </p><p>If you’re nervous because you hated the ending of <i>28 Years Later </i>(can’t relate), don’t be. Nia DaCosta didn’t go that route at all. </p><p>I’m so delighted with everything going on with this <i>Years</i> trilogy, it’s so thematically rich. <i>Bone Temple</i> starts seemingly moments after <i>28 Years Later </i>ended but couldn’t be more visually and tonally different. Director Nia DaCosta wasn’t interested in attempting to emulate Boyle’s camera or editing style in any way and even though it’s all born of an Alex Garland script it feels wholly original. </p><p>It’s both gross-out visceral and wildly hilarious, the latter is due to Jack O’Connell’s maniacally charismatic Jimmy Crystal. </p><p>What I love…</p> </div> </div> <div class="viewing-actions"> <div class="review-actions"> <p class="like-link-target react-component" data-component-class="LikeComponent" data-likeable-identifier='{"lid":"cvZbZB","uid":"viewing:1146624451","type":"viewing","typeName":"review"}' data-redacted="false" data-element-type="p" data-likes-page="/moviesrtherapy/film/28-years-later-the-bone-temple/likes/" data-format="count" data-count="6343" data-owner="MoviesRTherapy" > <span class="has-icon icon-16 icon-like"></span> </p> <button class="button-neue -text -small translation-button" hidden data-translation-control-for="cvZbZB" > <span class="label js-label"> Translate </span> </button> <div hidden class="translation-disclaimer js-translation-disclaimer"> Translated from <span class="js-language-name"></span> by <span class="js-translated-by"></span> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> </article> </div>
